text:
sara: Heads-up — tomorrow's 09:00 UTC deploy for model-serving v3.2 will include the latency patch. We need explicit backout steps and a pin policy in the runbook. Link: https://go/redwood/runbooks/model-serving-backout

jin: Thanks. Can you paste the minimal rollback command we'll use if the canary fails?

sara: Minimal rollback is basically pinning traffic back to v3.1 and reverting the config change. Quick snippet:
```bash
# pin all traffic to stable tag v3.1
redwoodctl routes pin --service model-serving --tag v3.1 --reason "rollback v3.2 canary"
# revert feature flag locally then apply
git checkout release/v3.1 && kubectl apply -f k8s/model-serving.yaml
```

mike: Where should SRE run that? Any dedicated emergency terminal?

sara: Oncall runbook says use the jumpbox in prod-subnet (jump-prod-1). Credentials in vault path: secret/prod/oncall/jumpbox. Prefer to run redwoodctl from the jumpbox to avoid IAM blips.

anya: For the canary threshold, are we still using 5%/5m error rate > 2% as auto-fail?

sara: Yes — canary policy: 5% traffic, 5m evaluation window. Auto-fail overrides if 95th latency > 800ms or error rate > 2%. Manual rollback if downstream rps drops >20% or customer errors spike. Documented in runbook.

deploy-bot: Canary started: model-serving:v3.2 -> 5% traffic. Canary time window: 09:00-09:05 UTC. Monitor: /dash/model-serving/canary (internal).

jin: If deploy-bot auto-fails, does it pin automatically?

sara: No — auto-fail triggers alert and marks the canary failed, but we require a human confirm for pin/revert. We do this to avoid flip-flopping during transient infra issues. The manual step is intentional.

release-coordinator: Adding two operational items to the runbook section: 1) checklist for quick pin (one-liner), 2) communication template for customers. I'll add them now.

mike: Suggestion: add a local smoke test script that runs post-pin to verify both latency and correctness (sample below).
```bash
# quick smoke check
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"model-serving","input":"ping"}' | jq '.status, .latency_ms'
```

anya: Also recommend a fast rollback branch policy: when we pin back to v3.1, create a short-lived branch release/hotfix-v3.1-rollback with the revert commit and tag it. That helps auditing.

sara: Good call. Logging/audit steps in runbook: create PR->merge to hotfix branch, tag with rollback timestamp, attach incident ID.

jin: One more: include exact runbook lines for customer-facing comms. Small template please — who handles that?

release-coordinator: I'll own the template. Draft: "We're pausing the v3.2 rollout while we investigate a regression. Traffic has been pinned to the stable v3.1. We'll post updates at 09:30 UTC."

mike: OK. I pushed a short section to the runbook with the rollback command, jumpbox path, and smoke test. Please sanity check.

anya: LGTM from my side. Agree to require two approvals for an unpin/redeploy to v3.2 after rollback.

sara: Decision: keep canary as-is tomorrow, oncall watches. If auto-fail or manual signal, SRE executes the pin snippet, run smoke, then release-coordinator sends customer template. After root-cause, we'll follow hotfix branch flow.

deploy-bot: Canary status: 09:03 UTC — metrics nominal, no alerts.

jin: Thanks everyone. I'll be oncall tomorrow and available during the change window.

sara: Thanks — leaving final runbook link here: https://go/redwood/runbooks/model-serving-backout (added checklist + templates). :thumbsup:
